items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I used to hang out there with them. I got to know all the boxers... I got to know him a little bit.

ctx.x: Birdland. He was staying down the hall from me, telling people that when I got famous, that he taught me all I know. He’s a funny little guy. Like I say, Dizzy and Lorraine, and Erroll Garner, and some other people that wasn’t that noteworthy lived in there, but they were entertainers. Right in between that building and the Teresa Hotel, Sugar Ray [Robinson] had his whole – owned the whole block there. He had a barber shop, a bar, a real estate office, a lot of stuff. That was his block. I used to hang out there…
Were you good with your hands?
